entries.title: CLI update: sponsored-account-prompt
entries.summary: CLI changes across 3 file(s) (+146/−5).

ai.title: Resolve bfcid slot in sponsored credential key links
ai.summary: Added `trackedSponsoredCredentials` to fill the `{bfcid}` slot in declared credential key-page URLs with the run's signed click id, mirroring Desktop and Cloud behavior. If no signed id is available, the link is dropped rather than shown with a literal placeholder, and the `{email}` slot is removed to prevent unauthorized email sharing. `SponsoredRun.startTurn` now passes runtime inputs to this resolver, and `SponsoredAccountPrompt` accepts an injectable `openUrl` handler so the resolved link is opened in the user's browser when clicked.
ai.evidence: New export `trackedSponsoredCredentials` in `cli/src/utils/sponsored-account-step.ts` maps declared credentials through `resolveSponsoredBfcidTemplate` and `signupUrlWithEmail`; `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts` now calls this function instead of passing raw `declaredRunCredentials` to the account step; `SponsoredAccountPrompt` accepts an injectable `openUrl` prop to render resolved key-page links.

eli5.text: When a sponsored task in the terminal assistant asks you to provide a login link, that link now includes a unique tracking code that identifies your specific session, ensuring the advertiser knows you came from this particular offer. If a tracking code is not available, the link is simply not shown rather than displaying a broken placeholder, and any field that would have sent your email address to the advertiser has been removed to protect your privacy. This affects developers using the free tier who run sponsored tasks in the terminal, and the visible result is a cleaner sign-in prompt that links directly to your session without sharing unnecessary personal details.

entries.title: CLI update: sponsored-account-prompt
entries.summary: New files: `common/src/ads/sponsored-run-links.ts`.

ai.title: Guard sponsored account links against unfilled click ids
ai.summary: This commit centralizes sponsored link resolution in the new `common/src/ads/sponsored-run-links.ts` module, replacing per-call-site logic with a single resolver that fills the signed click id into sign-up and credential key pages. The CLI's account prompt now applies a last-resort guard (`shownSponsoredLink`) that prevents any link containing a literal `{bfcid}` placeholder from being drawn or opened. When a link is blocked, the guard falls back to the Accept's signed advertiser link if available, or omits the link entirely, and emits the `UNFILLED_CLICK_ID_BLOCKED_METRIC` warning. This ensures sign-ups are always attributed and never routed to a placeholder URL, fixing a gap where the CLI key form could previously open an unattributed link.
ai.evidence: The new file `common/src/ads/sponsored-run-links.ts` introduces `resolveSponsoredRunLinks` and `guardSponsoredLink` to centralize link resolution. In `cli/src/components/sponsored-account-prompt.tsx`, the `TerminalLink` components for sign-in and credentials are now wrapped by a new `shownSponsoredLink` guard that blocks URLs matching the `UNFILLED_CLICK_ID` regex.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the server-side `resolvedLinks` field is already populated by all backend versions or if this is a staged rollout.

changes.what: Adds `sponsored-run-links.ts` with a central resolver and guard for sponsored account and credential links.
Updates `SponsoredAccountPrompt` to filter sign-in and credential links through the new guard before rendering or opening them.
Refactors `SponsoredAccountStep` to use the shared link resolver and guard instead of local credential tracking logic.
Extends the `SponsoredAccept` type to include an optional `resolvedLinks` field from the server.

eli5.text: A safeguard now prevents ad-powered tasks in the terminal app from showing you sign-up or key-entry links that lack a valid tracking identifier. If such an incomplete link is detected, the app will either use a valid backup link provided by the advertiser or hide the link entirely, ensuring you never click a broken connection. This improvement affects developers who use the free terminal app and accept sponsored tasks, giving you a more reliable experience when the app asks you to sign in or connect a service key.

ai.title: Extend external conversion postback telemetry with rail and identity
ai.summary: The `ads.external_conversion_postback` Axiom event in the `common` package now carries the authenticated `advertiser_id` and a new `selected_rail` field closed over `click_id`, `identity_email`, and `none`. Boolean presence flags (`email_present`, `email_hash_present`) and a validity flag (`email_hash_valid`) record whether canonical identity fields were supplied and accepted without logging the raw email or digest. A new export `ADS_EXTERNAL_CONVERSION_SELECTED_RAILS` defines the closed vocabulary, and `sanitizeExternalConversionPostbackFields` drops `selected_rail` values outside that set to keep the postback stream safe to aggregate.
ai.evidence: The diff in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` adds the `ADS_EXTERNAL_CONVERSION_SELECTED_RAILS` export and extends `ADS_EXTERNAL_CONVERSION_POSTBACK_FIELDS` with `advertiser_id`, `selected_rail`, `email_present`, `email_hash_present`, and `email_hash_valid` fields, plus sanitization logic that drops out-of-vocabulary `selected_rail` values.

entries.title: CLI update: index
entries.summary: CLI changes across 6 file(s) (+268/−64).

ai.title: CLI config and chat state files now use owner-only POSIX permissions
ai.summary: The CLI now enforces restrictive POSIX permissions on its configuration and data directories to prevent other users on a shared host from reading sensitive session data. A new `tightenConfigDirMode` function clamps the existing config directory to `0o700` at startup, while `ensureChatDirectory` and `saveMessageHistory` now create their respective directories and files with `0o700` and `0o600` modes. The `writeFileAtomic` and `writeFileAtomicAsync` helpers use a new `PRIVATE_FILE_MODE` constant to ensure that transient files for transcripts and run state are created as owner-only, replacing any previously world-readable files on rewrite.
ai.evidence: The diff introduces `tightenConfigDirMode` in `cli/src/utils/config-dir.ts` to clamp the config directory to `0o700`, and adds `PRIVATE_FILE_MODE` (`0o600`) to `cli/src/utils/write-file-atomic.ts` so that `writeFileAtomic` and `writeFileAtomicAsync` create temp files with owner-only permissions.

eli5.text: The CLI now locks down its private folders and files so that only you can read them, preventing other people who share the same computer from seeing your chat transcripts or typing history. This change applies to anyone using the Freebuff command-line tool on Mac or Linux, as Windows already handles these file permissions differently. You will not need to take any action, but if your older version left these files open to everyone on the machine, the tool will now automatically tighten their access the next time you start it.
